_meta.brand: KS Capital Partners — independent business introduction and advisory firm, Milan
_meta.house_style: Near-black editorial architectural photography. ONE warm directional light source (~2900-3200K), with a soft warm fill that keeps the shadows open and full of detail. Medium-format quality, 80mm equivalent, f/8, deep tonal separation, deep but open shadows (#16161c–#24242c), never blocked up, warm champagne-gold highlights (#c9a227–#d8b476), desaturated midtones. Quiet, private, expensive. No hype, no drama. Exposure is one to one and a half stops brighter than classic low-key: dark and luxurious, never murky.

_meta.note_openai: The OpenAI images endpoint has no negative-prompt parameter, so each `prompt` already ends with an explicit exclusion clause. The separate `negative` field is kept for Flux / SDXL / Midjourney portability (Midjourney: append as --no).
_meta.sizes: gpt-image-2 accepts 1536x1024 (3:2 landscape), 1024x1536 (2:3 portrait), 1024x1024. og-image is generated at 1536x1024 and cropped to 1200x630.
_meta.contrast_rule: No pixel beneath live type may be lighter than #1d1d20. At that ceiling the gold #c9a227 reads 6.9:1 and the bone #f2ede4 reads 14.3:1 against the plate — both clear AA, gold clears AAA for large display sizes.
_meta.contrast_measured: Measured on the procedural fallback at 1200px wide, sampling the whole text column (x 6-48%, y 30-62%): hero #181612 -> gold 7.5:1 / bone 15.5:1; about #111110 -> 7.8:1 / 16.2:1; network #2a2826 -> 6.1:1 / 12.6:1; og #0e0e0e -> 8.0:1 / 16.6:1. Re-run the same check after dropping photographs in: a photograph is brighter than the fallback it replaces.
_meta.alt_note: scripts/build.py marks every .art figure aria-hidden="true", so these plates are decorative and must ship with alt="". The alt strings here are held for any slot later promoted to content imagery; the strings that actually reach the reader are the section headings and the og_headline.

hero.prompt: A monumental dark stone corridor photographed straight down its axis, opening at the far end onto a calm sunlit sea horizon. Colossal fluted piers of honed dark grey limestone recede in perfect one-point perspective, their inner edges catching a thin warm rim of light. The far opening is a tall rectangular aperture filled with pale gold haze and a single clean sea horizon line. Low late-afternoon sun pours through it and spills in one long unbroken sheet across the polished stone floor, which reflects the aperture as a soft elongated smear. Ninety percent of the frame is in deep shadow; only the aperture, the floor spill and the rim-lit pier edges carry light. Colour: near-black stone at #0d0d0f, warm champagne highlights at #d8b476, no other hue. Medium-format architectural photography, 50mm, f/8, tripod, long exposure, perfectly level horizon, symmetrical composition with generous dark space at left and right for overlaid type. Subtle fine film grain, natural falloff, no artificial glow. Serene, silent, monumental, expensive. Do not include: people, figures, boats, birds, text, lettering, signage, logos, watermarks, furniture, plants, visible light fixtures, blue or cyan cast, HDR look, lens flare. Exposure sits between low-key and normal: the corridor stays genuinely dark, but the light from the far aperture is stronger and spreads much further — flooding down the floor toward the camera and washing warmly up the inner faces of the nearest piers, so the stone shows its grain in the mid-tones instead of going flat black. The stone is dark warm brown-grey, never cool grey, and the whole frame is unmistakably lit by a low golden sun. The left and right thirds must stay dark enough to carry white text over them.

focus-oil.prompt: Extreme close detail of the lid of a black steel oil drum, seen from a low three-quarter angle in warm, low but clearly readable light. The surface is wet: a thin film of water and oil beads across the matte black steel, and the concentric machine-rolled rings and the raised chime ring catch a single hard raking highlight from one warm light source at the upper right, drawing one bright crescent across the top edge and scattering tiny specular points through the beading. The bung plug sits off-centre, its threads dark and precise. Everything beyond the lit crescent falls to true black. Colour: black steel at #0b0b0c, one warm champagne specular at #e8d5a8, a faint amber sheen in the oil film, nothing else. Macro medium-format still life, 100mm, f/11, tack sharp on the lit rim, deep shadow occupying two thirds of the vertical frame. Fine film grain, industrial, restrained, no drama. Do not include: text, stencilled letters, hazard labels, numbers, logos, branding, watermarks, rust, dents, dirt, spills, people, hands, tools, blue or cyan highlights, coloured reflections, rainbow oil slick, HDR. Brighter overall exposure than a typical low-key photograph: the subject must read clearly on a phone screen in daylight. Keep the mood dark, warm and expensive, but open the shadows — full tonal range, luminous champagne highlights, visible material texture throughout, no blocked-up blacks. Add a soft secondary fill light at roughly a quarter of the key light's intensity so the form is fully described.

focus-art.prompt: Interior photograph of a private viewing room in a European collector's residence, in the evening. Vertical frame. A large old painting in a heavy, softly worn carved giltwood frame stands on a dark wooden easel, turned almost edge-on to the camera, so that the painted surface itself cannot be seen: only the depth of the gilded frame, its carved ornament and the dark back edge of the canvas stretcher are visible. A folded charcoal linen cloth hangs over the top corner of the frame. One narrow warm spotlight from high on the left grazes the gilding, which glows a muted champagne gold; everything else falls into deep, open shadow: dark walnut panelling behind, a parquet floor with a low sheen, the arm of a leather chair just catching the edge of the light. The frame and its light sit in the middle third of the image; the top and bottom fifths are calm, dark and uncluttered. Quiet and discreet, with the quality of a museum but none of its apparatus. Full-frame camera, 50mm lens, f/4, realistic exposure with open shadows and gentle highlight roll-off, subtle film grain, true-to-life texture: it must read as a real photograph, not a render. Do not include: the painted image or any recognisable artwork, people, faces, hands, text, wall labels, price tags, logos, white gallery walls, visible spotlights or lamps, glass cases, ropes, HDR, oversaturated colour, blue or teal cast, CGI or 3D-render look.

focus-stone.prompt: The corner of a single monolithic block of travertine, filling the frame, photographed close in a dark quarry yard at dusk. Two sawn faces meet at a crisp vertical arris: the left face takes a warm low raking light that rakes across the stone and reveals its horizontal bedding, open pores, and the fine parallel striations left by the gang saw; the right face falls away into deep shadow and reads almost black. The top chamfer catches one thin bright edge. The travertine is warm cream and biscuit, banded in ivory, ochre and pale grey, weighty and matte. Background is featureless darkness. Colour: cream #d9cdb6 in the light, #14120f in the shadow, warm throughout, no cool tones. Medium-format still life, 80mm, f/11, vertical, the block cropped by all four edges to feel monumental. Fine film grain, tactile, geological, silent. Do not include: people, machinery, forklifts, cranes, tools, cables, text, stencilled numbers, quarry markings, chalk marks, logos, watermarks, polished or shiny surfaces, sky, vegetation, dust haze, blue cast, HDR. Brighter overall exposure than a typical low-key photograph: the subject must read clearly on a phone screen in daylight. Keep the mood dark, warm and expensive, but open the shadows — full tonal range, luminous champagne highlights, visible material texture throughout, no blocked-up blacks. Add a soft secondary fill light at roughly a quarter of the key light's intensity so the form is fully described.

about.prompt: Editorial interior photograph, as if commissioned for a Swiss private bank's annual report. The private meeting room of a nineteenth-century palazzo in central Milan, late afternoon in winter. Vertical frame, camera at standing eye height just inside the doorway, looking down the length of the room. A long, dark walnut table runs from the lower edge of the frame into depth, with dark leather chairs pushed in neatly; its waxed surface holds a soft reflection of the windows and nothing else. Along the left wall, two tall windows with sheer off-white linen curtains let in soft, low, slightly warm daylight that falls across the table and onto a honed grey-beige limestone floor. At the far end of the room, beside the second window, two people in dark charcoal tailored clothes, a man and a woman, stand close together in quiet conversation, seen from behind in three-quarter back view, partly in silhouette against the window light. They are small in the frame, occupying less than a fifth of its height, and slightly soft, because the focus is on the room. Their faces are not visible. Dark oak boiserie panelling with a restrained carved cornice; a large unlit fireplace in warm grey stone on the right wall; a pair of bronze wall sconces, switched off. The two figures sit in the upper-middle part of the frame, around 40% from the top; the bottom fifth is the dark near end of the table. Palette: black, charcoal, warm stone, dark brown, muted beige, champagne highlights; low saturation, no bright colour anywhere. Full-frame camera, 35mm lens, f/4, natural light only, realistic exposure with open shadows and gentle highlight roll-off, subtle film grain, true-to-life material texture and small real-world imperfections: it must read as a real photograph, not a render. Do not include: handshakes, people facing the camera, faces, smiling or posing people, laptops, phones, screens, charts, papers with text, money, logos, text, signage, a city view or skyline through the windows (the windows show only diffused light), globes, maps, flowers, plants, clutter, HDR, CGI or 3D-render look, plastic skin, oversaturated colour, blue or teal cast.

network.prompt: Architectural landscape photograph from the stone terrace of a private villa on the Mediterranean coast, at dusk. Horizontal frame. On the right, the end of a weathered limestone balustrade with a few turned balusters, lit warmly by the last light, and the corner of a stone terrace floor. Beyond it, a calm sea meets the horizon in a soft, hazy line; the sky fades from deep warm grey at the top to a muted champagne glow at the horizon. The left two thirds of the frame are open sky and sea with almost no detail: a quiet gradient. No sun disc, no boats, no coastline buildings, no people. cta-texture.prompt: A flat-on surface study of a slab of very dark stone, filling the entire frame edge to edge: black basalt-toned marble, honed rather than polished, with sparse pale veining that drifts diagonally across the field in thin irregular filaments and one broader vein that fades before it reaches the corner. The surface is lit by one broad soft warm light from the upper left, giving a slow luminance gradient from a faint warm sheen at top-left to near-total black at bottom-right, with no hotspot and no specular glare. The grain is fine and even; the veins are bone and pale ochre, never white, never blue. Absolutely flat perspective, no edges of the slab visible, no depth, no objects. Colour: #0c0c0e to #1a1a1d with #cbb98f veining. Medium-format copy-stand photography, 90mm, f/11, evenly exposed, tileable feel, moderately low overall contrast so it can sit behind type. Fine film grain. Do not include: slab edges, corners, joints, grout, objects, tools, hands, text, logos, watermarks, reflections, highlights, hotspots, glare, glossy polish, water, blue or grey-blue veining, white veining, high contrast, dramatic lighting, vignette. Keep this one restrained: it sits behind text at low opacity. Slightly more visible veining and material than a pure black slab, but overall still dark and even, with no bright hotspot anywhere.

Colour: #0a0a0b shadow, #d8b476 light, nothing else.
